Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related technical field; Master’s degree a plus.

Server-Sent Events (SSE), conversational chat UIs, and multi-modal content displays.
trong command of modern CSS, state management (Zustand, Redux Toolkit, or Jotai), and UI component libraries.

Who You Are
First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?"
Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.
Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.
What You'll Bring
1+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.
Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.
Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.
Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.

From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.
At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.
The NPI team is seeking a
Equipment Controls Engineer
—a highly motivated individual responsible for developing, programming, commissioning, and optimizing new R&D test fixtures and automated systems to support new product development and high-volume production ramp-up. This cross-disciplinary role bridges mechanical, electrical, and software engineering to deliver practical, reliable, and efficient systems that meet design intent and operational goals.
This is a full-time, on-site position based in Fremont, CA, requiring presence in the office five days a week.
Key Responsibilities:
Setup, program and test control systems to support Process Development and Manufacturing processes
Utilize industrial communication protocols to enable reliable data exchange between systems
Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance system reliability and scalability
Lead and support commissioning activities with cross-functional teams

Repurpose and upgrade existing equipment for feasibilities and proof-of-concept efforts.
Partner with Operations to support new product introduction (NPI) and high-volume production ramp-up
Document and transfer automation processes to Operations
Train team members during new equipment handoff and support release of the new equipment to ensure smooth transition from NPI to Operations.

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Controls Engineering or related discipline
0-2 years of experience in industrial automation and system integration
Experience with Allen Bradley PLC ladder logic programming and ability to pick up new programming languages as needed

Good written and verbal communication
Highly motivated self-starter, capable of organizing and working independently and manage tasks with minimal oversight

description_preview:
We're looking for an
Infrastructure Engineer
to own the execution layer beneath our RL environments: the systems that let an agent operate inside a realistic, multi-tool world coherently for hours or days.
This is a hard systems problem disguised as an AI job.
As the tasks agents can complete keep lengthening, the environments that train them have to stay coherent across far longer horizons than anything that exists today.
That means sandboxing and isolation you can trust, execution that's fast and cheap enough to run at training scale, and the ability to snapshot, restore, inspect, and branch a running environment instead of treating every rollout as one-shot. You'll build the platform that makes all of this possible.
You'll work closely with our research and data teams, and directly with frontier labs and enterprise customers, to turn environment designs into infrastructure that runs reliably in production.
What You'll Do
Environment Execution & Sandboxing:
Design and own the sandboxing and execution layer that environments run inside. Build systems to snapshot and restore environment state (disk, process, and where relevant memory and accelerator state) so runs can be paused, resumed, inspected, and branched rather than executed once.
Develop the machinery to detect failure modes early in a rollout (reward hacks, infra faults, fairness issues) and to revert to a known-good state, patch, and continue.
Extend execution to long-horizon and multi-node environments, where an agent operates across many tools and services over hours or days.
Performance & Scale
Own the performance characteristics of the platform: throughput, latency, and cost-per-rollout at scale.
Drive utilization and scheduling so we can run far more environment rollouts per dollar without sacrificing reliability.
Profile and remove bottlenecks across the stack, from container startup to environment teardown.
Build the observability that lets us understand what's happening inside thousands of concurrent, long-running rollouts.
Environment Platform
Build and maintain the framework for specifying, packaging, and deploying RL environments which is used by both humans and agents authoring environments internally.
Create the tooling that lets researchers and environment authors debug a specific failure across hundreds of long agent traces.
Deploy large / small models on on-prem hardware
Collaboration & Production Excellence
Scale prototypes into production systems with reproducible workflows and high engineering standards.
Write the documentation and tools that let internal teams and external users build on the platform.
What We're Looking For
Systems & Infrastructure
Strong track record building production systems or research infrastructure at scale: distributed systems, execution engines, container/sandboxing infrastructure, or similar.
Deep comfort with the systems layer: containers and isolation (e.g. namespaces, cgroups, VMs, gVisor/Firecracker-style sandboxing), filesystems, process and state management.
Experience making systems fast and cheap — profiling, scheduling, resource utilization, and cost optimization at scale.
Proficiency with cloud platforms (GCP, AWS) and distributed computing.
Strong engineering fundamentals and a systematic approach to testing, validation, and reliability.
Experience of deploying large / small models on on-prem hardware
Execution & Ownership
Comfort operating in ambiguity.
Strong Python skills; comfort in a systems language (Rust, Go, or C++) is a plus.
Ability to use modern tools such as Claude Code effectively.
Collaboration & Communication
Excellent communication skills for working with research teams and enterprise customers.
Ability to translate between research needs and infrastructure requirements.
Comfortable presenting technical work to diverse audiences.

Capital One is a leading financial services company committed to transforming banking through innovative technology and responsible AI practices. With a longstanding reputation for leveraging machine learning and data analytics, Capital One strives to deliver personalized, real-time experiences that meet the evolving needs of its customers. The company invests heavily in cutting-edge infrastructure and attracts top-tier talent to maintain its position at the forefront of AI-driven financial solutions. Capital One’s mission is to create a more inclusive and accessible banking environment by harnessing the power of emerging AI capabilities, ultimately changing how banking services are delivered and experienced worldwide.
About The Role
The Lead AI Engineer role at Capital One is a strategic position focused on advancing the company's AI foundations, large language model (LLM) core, and agentic AI systems. As a key member of the Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams to design, develop, and deploy sophisticated AI solutions that revolutionize customer interactions and internal processes. Your expertise will drive innovations in foundation model training, inference, similarity search, and AI governance, ensuring the scalability, efficiency, and ethical deployment of AI systems. This role offers an exciting opportunity to shape the future of responsible AI in banking, working on high-impact projects that serve millions of customers and support business growth.
Qualifications
The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical background combined with a passion for innovation in AI. A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, or related fields, along with at least 4 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms, is required. Alternatively, a master's degree with a minimum of 2 years of relevant experience will also be considered. Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Go, Scala, or Java is essential. Candidates should demonstrate a solid understanding of hardware and software optimization, large-scale AI deployment, and familiarity with cloud platforms like AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure. A deep curiosity for AI research, the ability to translate scientific publications into practical solutions, and strong problem-solving skills are highly valued.
Responsibilities
Partner with multidisciplinary teams, including engineers, research scientists, product managers, and program leads, to deliver state-of-the-art AI-powered products that enhance customer experience and operational efficiency.
Design, develop, test, and support AI software components, including foundation model training, large language model inference, similarity search, guardrails, and observability frameworks.
Leverage a broad stack of open-source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, Nemo Guardrails, and PyTorch to build scalable AI solutions.
Invent and implement advanced optimization techniques for large language models to improve performance metrics such as scalability, latency, throughput, and cost-efficiency in production environments.
Contribute to the technical vision and long-term roadmap of foundational AI systems, ensuring alignment with business objectives and responsible AI practices.
Continuously stay updated with the latest AI research and incorporate innovative techniques into production systems.
Ensure AI systems adhere to governance, ethical standards, and regulatory requirements, maintaining transparency and fairness.
Benefits
Capital One offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and professional growth. This includes competitive salaries, performance-based incentives, health insurance plans, retirement savings options, and paid time off. Employees have access to ongoing learning opportunities, career development programs, and a collaborative work environment that fosters innovation. The company emphasizes diversity and inclusion, providing a supportive atmosphere for all employees. Additionally, flexible work arrangements and wellness initiatives are available to help balance personal and professional commitments.
Equal Opportunity
Capital One is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We believe that a diverse workforce enhances our ability to innovate and serve our customers effectively. We are dedicated to providing a work environment where all employees are valued, respected, and given equal opportunities to succeed. Furthermore, Capital One complies with all applicable laws and regulations related to non-discrimination and equal employment opportunities.

description_preview:
The backbone of any technology org is its infrastructure, come join the team giving that skeleton superhuman abilities. The Infrastructure team at Mercury is an enablement lever for the rest of the business, building scaleable, secure and maintainable foundations for the rest of the org to build on top of.
Infrastructure is currently building out more platform features to make it easier for agents and humans to deploy code. This means security by default, observable by default and easy to use and operate. We do all this while not compromising on speed, and ship to prod all day, every day, which is a testament to the strong foundations this team has built.
We are looking for an engineer to join our team to help build out the “platform” even further! We maintain everything from networking to container orchestration, and work with product teams to enable any AWS needs they have. We want someone who is passionate about building maintainable systems, is obsessed with quality and making sure the sharp edges are filed off, and is extremely helpful when diving into problems with our product counterparts.
This is a role for someone who likes going deep, shipping often, and leaving systems better than they found them. Someone who cares about quality without turning quality into bureaucracy. Someone who is just as happy debugging a strange Linux problem as they are helping a product engineer understand why their service behaves differently in production.
Some of the technology you’ll work with
Our infrastructure is built primarily on AWS, including systems like EC2, RDS, OpenSearch, ECS, and EKS. We like to use the right tool for the job and bias towards cloud native open source tooling
We use Terraform extensively to manage infrastructure as code, GitHub and GitHub Actions for version control and delivery, and Prometheus, Grafana, OpenSearch, and OpenTelemetry to understand what is happening in production.
We’re also increasingly building
agentic infrastructure
: systems that let AI agents safely interact with our infrastructure, and frameworks that give both agents and the humans operating them the right guardrails.
You do not need to arrive knowing every tool we use. We care more about strong fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to go deep.
As we gear up for the next stages of Mercury's growth, you will:
Build our “Infrastructure Platform” to support the growing needs of the Engineering Organization
Focus on building a platform that is AI friendly while still usable for engineers. We want our users to be humans and Agents
Deliver key infrastructure projects, break-down complex initiatives, and define our infrastructure strategy through detailed RFCs and technical specifications
Must haves:
You have 2+ years of experience with AWS
You have a keen interest in cloud native open source technologies, and feel comfortable contributing code upstream to these technologies
Strong knowledge of low-level operating system foundations (linux, file systems, containers, etc)
You have demonstrated ability in technical writing, with at least 2 years of experience creating detailed technical documentation, RFCs, and tech specs that clearly communicate complex ideas
The ideal candidate should:
Be used to operating in regulated environments such as HITRUST or SOC2, ensuring compliance and security
Have 2+ years of experience working in massive terraform environments, with many engineers contributing code in a scalable way
Have 2+ years of experience writing code. We are building an Infrastructure Platform from scratch and there is plenty of code to write to support that
Be extremely willing to learn and dive into hard problems! We have many to solve!
The Infrastructure team sits in an interesting place at Mercury: close enough to production that the details matter, and broad enough that a good abstraction can make hundreds of engineers faster.
There is a lot left to build.
If you like infrastructure that is secure by default, observable by default, pleasant to use, and designed for people who want to ship, we’d love to hear from you.

As a mobile developer, you’ll help build and support the ServeManager mobile app for iOS and Android. You’ll work alongside our current mobile developers so the team has more coverage across feature work, bug fixes, releases, and day-to-day app support.
The app supports process servers and firms in the field, so much of the work is practical and workflow-driven: jobs, attempts, routing, uploads, notifications, documents, signatures, and account tools. You’ll work with product, design team (UI/UX), backend, stakeholders, and support to keep those workflows reliable, easy to use, and ready for release
This is a hybrid role, with in-office days on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays at our Denver office.
Compensation
This role offers a competitive compensation range of $96,480 to $135,000, depending on experience, skills, and internal equity.
About InfoTrack
InfoTrack is a platform that seamlessly connects law firms to the courts and to the services that they need to litigate successfully. We're global leaders in legal technology with unparalleled expertise in forging integrations that can drastically improve the efficiency of law firms and the legal system.
As a highly ambitious company, we know that our people are critical to our success. That's why we're passionate about fostering a high-performance culture built on professional development, open communication, and transparent leadership. If you're smart, dedicated, and eager to help build a market-leading solution that makes a difference in the lives of our clients, join us.

Develop and maintain features in the ServeManager iOS and Android app
Work with product, design team (UI/UX), backend, stakeholders, and support to improve mobile workflows and meet roadmap goals
Share ownership of the mobile app with the current mobile team so releases and support do not depend on one person
Build clear, practical screens for field users based on real user needs and workflows
Support core app areas such as jobs, attempts, routing, uploads, notifications, documents, signatures, and account tools
Connect the app to ServeManager APIs and third-party services as needed
Test changes on simulators, emulators, and real devices before release
Help prepare and validate TestFlight, Google Play internal testing, App Store, and Google Play releases
Troubleshoot production issues, crash reports, performance problems, and device-specific bugs
Maintain existing mobile code, including iOS and Android-specific behavior
Review mobile code from other developers and give practical feedback
Keep key mobile setup, release, and support steps documented for team coverage
Follow secure mobile development practices around user data, account access, API communication, and app permissions
Use approved AI tools to improve productivity with development, testing, debugging, and code review while maintaining quality and security

3+ years of experience building and maintaining production mobile apps released to the Apple App Store and Google Play
Strong React Native, TypeScript, and modern JavaScript experience
Comfortable debugging iOS and Android issues with real devices, simulators, emulators, Xcode, and Android Studio
Experience with REST APIs, authentication, file uploads, third-party integrations, and async app workflows

Experience using AI tools to improve development speed, testing, debugging, or code review is a plus

At InfoTrack, we’re committed to a workplace where everyone feels comfortable doing their best work and having fun! We're hiring a
Front End Engineer
— not a designer who occasionally codes, and not an engineer who occasionally opens Figma. This person is equally comfortable defining the interaction model for a new feature and shipping the React that powers it. You'll be the first dedicated front end engineering hire at Coinflow, which means you're not inheriting a design system — you're building it.
You'll work directly with the CTO and founding engineers, moving from rough product idea to shipped, polished UI without a handoff in between.

Build and own our design system on top of shadcn/ui and Tailwind — components, tokens, patterns, and documentation that the rest of engineering can build on without asking you first.
Design and ship full features end-to-end: wireframe or go straight to high-fidelity, build the actual production component, wire it to real data, and iterate based on how it feels in practice.
Redesign and modernize existing surfaces — merchant onboarding, dashboards, checkout flows — that were built for speed, not polish.
Set the visual direction for a fintech product that needs to feel trustworthy, fast, and precise — this is a payments platform, not a consumer app, and the design language should reflect that.
Make architecture decisions about component composition, theming, and reusability that will hold up as the product surface area grows.
Collaborate closely with backend engineers to make sure the front end accurately represents genuinely complex systems (multi-chain settlement, card networks, fraud/risk states) without dumbing them down.

Strong command of shadcn/ui, Radix primitives, Tailwind CSS, and React/TypeScript — you should be able to talk through why shadcn's composition model works the way it does, not just how to install components.
A portfolio or GitHub history showing products you designed and built yourself, start to finish — not just Dribbble shots or isolated component libraries.
Real product design judgment: typography, spacing, color systems, information hierarchy, and the ability to simplify complex, data-heavy interfaces (we're a payments and financial infrastructure product).
Comfort owning ambiguity — you'll often be the one deciding what the right interaction pattern is, not implementing someone else's spec.
Experience building or significantly extending a design system in a real production codebase, including versioning, theming, and documentation practices that scale past one person using it.
Bonus: experience in fintech, crypto, or other data-dense, trust-sensitive product categories.
Bonus: familiarity with Next.js, React Native, or motion/animation libraries (Framer Motion, GSAP).
How We Work
Small team, high trust, low process. You'll ship things that go live within days, not sprints. We care much more about taste and craft holding up under real usage than about pixel-perfect specs that never ship.

In addition, the employee who fills this role will be eligible for an equity grant, allowing you to share in the long-term success of the company. You will also have access to a wide array of benefits, including health and wellness benefits, 401(k) savings plan, and flexible time off.
Join the team rewriting how money moves worldwide—and become a driving force in the $194 trillion cross-border payments market.

description_preview:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
APPLICATION SOFTWARE ENGINEER, APPLIED AI
The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.
In this Applied AI role within the Application Software team, you will design, evaluate, deploy, and integrate modern AI systems—including large language models and agentic systems—that power products and infrastructure across SpaceX. You will own the end-to-end lifecycle of AI capabilities from prototype to production while partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Operations teams. We are looking for a strong software engineer with a proven track record of delivering AI products, including hands-on experience evaluating, deploying, and integrating AI solutions into real production systems.
Aerospace experience is not required – rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers with diverse perspectives to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.
Responsibilities
Develop highly reliable software solutions used across SpaceX, including AI-powered applications that accelerate production, flight, and Starlink operations
Create new applications that improve how SpaceX operates by incorporating modern large language models, agentic systems, and other AI capabilities
Own the full lifecycle of Applied AI systems: design, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration from prototype to production
Deep dive into users’ problems to uncover high-leverage AI opportunities and deliver efficient, production-grade solutions
Architect production systems for agentic workflows, tool-use, multi-agent orchestration, advanced retrieval, and long-context applications that prioritize reliability, safety, and responsible deployment
Build and maintain rigorous evaluation frameworks (LLM-as-judge, automated benchmarks, online evaluation) and production observability/monitoring for AI quality, safety, latency, and cost
Stay at the frontier of LLM techniques and rapidly incorporate emerging best practices into production systems across SpaceX programs
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree
1+ years of experience in full stack development
Preferred Skills And Experience
Hands-on experience evaluating, deploying, and integrating AI models into production systems
Proven track record of delivering (or significantly contributing to) end-to-end AI products or production AI-powered features
Proven track record of shipping real-world AI products from prototype through production deployment and iteration
Deep hands-on experience with modern LLM techniques: agentic systems, tool-use / function calling, multi-agent orchestration, advanced retrieval architectures, fine-tuning, and structured outputs
Experience building production evaluation systems (LLM-as-judge, automated eval harnesses, A/B testing, red-teaming) and AI observability/monitoring (tracing, quality metrics, safety, cost)
Experience designing and implementing production architecture for AI-powered applications with strong emphasis on reliability, safety, and responsible deployment
Previous experience in AI product design, development, integration, testing, and productionization
Strong software engineering foundation with expertise in designing production systems (including AI-powered and system-to-system architectures) and a track record of writing clean, maintainable code
Programming experience in Python, C#.NET, Go, Scala, Java, or similar
Production experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and modern data streaming (Kafka or similar)

About TruckSmarter
TruckSmarter is building the operating system for the people who move the world’s freight.
Trucking is a massive, dynamic network: hundreds of thousands of carriers, tens of thousands of brokers, volatile prices, uncertain supply and demand, real-world constraints, and decisions made in minutes. Building products for it requires solving hard problems at the intersection of AI, mathematics, distributed systems, and product engineering working together.
We are looking for engineers who are excited by problems that do not have established patterns or obvious solutions. We value intellectual honesty, independent thinking, technical excellence, urgency, and ownership.
You will join a small team with experience building and scaling products at DoorDash, Uber Freight, LinkedIn, Affirm, Typeface, Flexport, Coinbase, and Strava.
What You'll Do
You will be given an important, ambiguous problem and expected to understand it deeply, formulate it precisely, explore possible approaches, and build a solution that works in the real world
Work directly with customers to uncover the real problem, not merely the requested feature.
Turn ambiguous objectives into models, algorithms, system designs, and measurable success criteria.
Build intelligent decision systems using optimization, probability, machine learning, information retrieval, graph algorithms, and related techniques.
Turn sophisticated mathematical and technical capabilities into products that are simple and intuitive to the people using them.
Design scalable, low-latency, fault-tolerant systems that operate across long-running and highly concurrent workflows.
Raise the technical standards through rigorous thinking, clear communication, thoughtful design reviews, and high-quality implementation.
The problems you will solve
Examples Of The Problems Our Engineers Work On Include
Building autonomous agents that can create plans, execute them over hours or days, react to rapidly changing market conditions, and know when an objective has been achieved or is no longer possible.
Searching and personalized ranking hundreds of thousands of freight opportunities against multiple, sometimes competing constraints in under a second.
Designing systems that balance exploration of new strategies with exploitation of approaches known to work.
Resolving incomplete, ambiguous, or contradictory information about locations, loads, companies, people, times, and prices.
Coordinating concurrent workflows while enforcing fairness, resource limits, permissions, and safety constraints.
What We're Looking For
We care more about intellectual ability, technical depth, and demonstrated achievement than about matching a rigid checklist.
You’ll Be a Strong Fit If You
Have an exceptional foundation in computer science, mathematics, statistics, physics, operations research, or another quantitative field.
Decompose messy, ambiguous problems into precise, tractable ones.
Move naturally between mathematical reasoning and production engineering.
Have built technically demanding systems, algorithms, infrastructure, or products.
Evaluate ideas rigorously through proofs, simulations, prototypes, benchmarks, experiments, and production data.
Learn unfamiliar domains quickly, communicate precisely, and want substantial ownership.
Communicate complex ideas precisely and can collaborate productively with other highly capable people.
You might come from a technology company, quant firm, research lab, ambitious startup, or rigorous academic program. Pedigree matters far less than how you think and what you’ve built.

You want to work with people who will challenge you.
You want difficult problems with real-world consequences.
You want the freedom and responsibility to find the right answer—not simply implement a spec.
And you want to build systems that can reshape how a massive industry operates.

We work in-person 5 days a week at our downtown San Francisco office. We believe the best products get built when people are in the same room. Fast feedback loops, real collaboration, and a team that genuinely enjoys working together. If that's how you do your best work, you'll fit right in.

About TruckSmarter
TruckSmarter is building the operating system for the people who move the world’s freight.
Trucking is a massive, dynamic network: hundreds of thousands of carriers, tens of thousands of brokers, volatile prices, uncertain supply and demand, real-world constraints, and decisions made in minutes. Building products for it requires solving hard problems at the intersection of AI, mathematics, distributed systems, and product engineering working together.
We are looking for engineers who are excited by problems that do not have established patterns or obvious solutions. We value intellectual honesty, independent thinking, technical excellence, urgency, and ownership.
You will join a small team with experience building and scaling products at DoorDash, Uber Freight, LinkedIn, Affirm, Typeface, Flexport, Coinbase, and Strava.
What You'll Do
You will be given important, ambiguous problems and expected to understand them deeply, evaluate possible approaches, and build solutions that work in the real world.
Work with customers and teammates to understand the underlying problem, not merely the requested feature.
Turn ambiguous objectives into clear technical approaches, system designs, and measurable success criteria.
Build intelligent systems using techniques such as optimization, probability, machine learning, information retrieval, graph algorithms, and related methods.
Turn sophisticated mathematical and technical capabilities into products that are simple and intuitive for the people using them.
Design and build reliable, scalable systems that support long-running and concurrent workflows.
Contribute to strong technical standards through thoughtful design, clear communication, constructive reviews, and high-quality implementation.
The problems you will solve
Examples Of The Problems Our Engineers Work On Include
Building autonomous agents that can create plans, execute them over hours or days, react to rapidly changing market conditions, and know when an objective has been achieved or is no longer possible.
Searching and personalized ranking hundreds of thousands of freight opportunities against multiple, sometimes competing constraints in under a second.
Designing systems that balance exploration of new strategies with exploitation of approaches known to work.
Resolving incomplete, ambiguous, or contradictory information about locations, loads, companies, people, times, and prices.
Coordinating concurrent workflows while enforcing fairness, resource limits, permissions, and safety constraints.
What We're Looking For
We care more about intellectual ability, technical depth, and demonstrated achievement than about matching a rigid checklist.
You’ll Be a Strong Fit If You
Have a strong foundation in computer science, mathematics, statistics, physics, operations research, or another quantitative field.
Can break down messy, ambiguous problems into clear, tractable ones.
Are comfortable moving between mathematical reasoning and production engineering.
Have built technically challenging systems, algorithms, infrastructure, or products.
Evaluate ideas rigorously using simulations, prototypes, benchmarks, experiments, production data, and other appropriate methods.
Learn unfamiliar domains quickly and take ownership of complex problems from approach through implementation.
Communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate productively with other highly capable people.
You should join us if
You want to work with people who will challenge you.
You want difficult problems with real-world consequences.
You want the freedom and responsibility to find the right answer—not simply implement a spec.
And you want to build systems that can reshape how a massive industry operates.
